summary: Fire tower at Sphene Lake, Rainy River District; a fan-run still-standing list names a Sphene Lake Tower near Rainy Lake, not confirmed as this tower, and no source confirms its condition or the 1924 date in a video title.

facts.status_note: Named as 'Sphene Lake Tower- Rainy Lake' on an undated fan-run still-standing list, which does not confirm it is this tower; no source we found confirms its condition since.

access.note: Remote lake. The former camp land is owned by Rainy River First Nations, and no source says whether the tower stands on it. The fan-run list asks visitors not to climb.

visit.trail_note: Remote: the camp tribute describes the lake as reached by water, air, winter ice and, at times, rough logging roads. No source describes a route to the tower.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific sources are the firelookout.ca record (no type, height, year or status), one undated fan-run still-standing list, and a camp tribute page. The 1924 date appears only in a 2015 video title on the tribute page, which was not opened; treat it as unconfirmed. The tribute mentions a second video (2023) and a research dossier that were not read. The firelookout.ca record also links a video by Rob Farrow (youtu.be/3LNnY-IV3oc), not opened. Name variants: Rainy River (firelookout.ca), Rainy Lake (fan list), Rainy River District (tribute). The story assumes the fan-list entry and the firelookout.ca record refer to the same tower. No source gives the tower's location relative to the camp buildings.
